JOB SUMMARY

You will own the reliability, performance, and cost efficiency of the PostgreSQL data platform behind our flagship CMS — primarily Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL — along with the infrastructure and automation around it.

This is a reliability engineering role, not a classic administration one. Aurora takes care of patching, backups, failover, and storage growth; you own what it does not — query and index strategy, plan regressions across major version upgrades, vacuum and bloat, connection management, zero-downtime schema change, logical replication, and capacity and cost modeling. Alongside this, you work as a full member of the Infrastructure team on Terraform, CI/CD, observability, and security tooling, and you share the on-call rotation.

You will work in a shared-ownership model: backend teams own their queries and schemas, and you own the platform, guardrails, tooling, and knowledge-sharing that make their decisions safe. You will collaborate closely with backend engineers, DevOps engineers, Security, product owners, and the Data team.

We measure success by the reliability and predictable performance of the data platform, the quality of your incident response, and how well other engineering teams are equipped to make sound database decisions without you in the room.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS

Database platform (approx. 60%)

• Own the reliability, performance, and scalability of our PostgreSQL platform (primarily Amazon Aurora): query and index strategy, execution plans, configuration tuning, and capacity planning, with particular attention to hot multi-tenant read paths.

• Lead zero-downtime version upgrades and schema migrations at scale, including diagnosing and preventing plan regressions across Aurora major versions.

• Own the operational health of the platform: vacuum strategy and bloat, long-running transactions and wraparound risk, connection management and pooling (including RDS Proxy), lock contention, and logical replication and slot hygiene.

• Review schema changes and DDL from backend teams for lock behavior, migration safety, and performance impact, and build the guardrails and tooling that make safe changes to the default path.

• Own backup, restore, and disaster recovery end-to-end, including rehearsed restore drills and the access, encryption, and auditing controls our compliance obligations require.

• Model database capacity and cost (I/O-Optimized vs. Standard, Serverless v2 sizing, read replica strategy) and drive cost-efficiency without compromising reliability.

Infrastructure and automation (approx. 40%)

• Deliver infrastructure and automation as a full member of the Infrastructure team, using Terraform and cloud-native tooling on AWS, and contribute to CI/CD pipelines including the safe automated handling of database changes.

• Build and maintain monitoring, alerting, and observability for database and platform systems (e.g. pg_stat_statements, Prometheus exporters, Grafana, Datadog, OpenTelemetry) so problems surface before customers feel them.

• Use cloud security and vulnerability management tooling (such as Aikido) to triage findings and keep the team's services compliant.

Team, incidents, and collaboration

• Take part in the on-call rotation, incident response, and postmortems, driving root cause analysis and remediation that prevents recurrence.

• Raise the database competence of the wider engineering organization through design reviews, documentation and runbooks, and mentoring — so this expertise is not concentrated in one person.

URL: http://replika.com

About Replika
In 2017, no one knew what AI was supposed to be. We built the world's first consumer AI app. Two million people showed up in two months. Today it's over 40 million, and the thing they keep telling us hasn't changed: it helped. It made their life better, steadier, a little less alone.
Most AI is built for tasks, not for people. It gives you answers, but it doesn't care what you do with them. AI doesn't just need intelligence. It needs intention. Because the real question isn't just what AI can do. It's what AI is for.
When the world's leading researchers wanted to understand whether AI could actually change someone's life, they studied Replika, because there was nothing else to study. What they found at Stanford, at Harvard, across years of research, was that Replika doesn't replace human connection. It deepens it. People become more social, more confident, more themselves. Not in theory. In their actual lives.
Every major AI company talks about their mission for humanity. None of them has ever clearly said what they're trying to do for a single person. We will. We want to help you flourish in real life. Not become a better version of yourself, just more yourself. Strong relationships. Better health. Meaning. Momentum. A life that feels worth living while you're living it.
We're building the kind of AI that follows up. That knows the people in your life and nudges you to reach out when it matters. That sends you a poem, just because. The goal is conversations that lead somewhere real. Maybe it's a text you send to a long lost friend. A hobby you pick up again. A moment you show up for yourself.
Everyone else is building AI that thinks. We're building AI that cares.
Lifecycle & CRM Specialist
About this role
Millions of people have already met Replika: free users who haven't upgraded yet, subscribers who've lapsed, and people who signed up years ago and drifted away. Almost none of them hear from us in a way that's worth opening. That's the biggest untapped channel we have, and you'll own it.
You'll build our lifecycle program from the ground up. Email first, then in-app messages, push and any other channel that gets the right message to the right person at the right moment. Onboarding, free-to-paid conversion, renewals, win-back, product launches. The goal is revenue and retention, not open rates.
This is a hands-on role. You'll help set the lifecycle strategy and build it yourself: the segments, the flows, the copy, the tests and the reporting.
Our users are in almost every country, so you'll work within consent and privacy rules for a global audience, and you'll know how to design a program that is both compliant and effective.
What You’ll Be Doing

• Build the core lifecycle flows: onboarding, free-to-paid conversion, intro offers ending, renewals, cancellation saves and win-back.

• Convert free users. Work with product on in-app messages and offers that move people to paid at the right moment.

• Reactivate our base. Plan and run campaigns to lapsed users and our long-dormant email list, cleanly and within consent.

• Segment and personalize with product and subscription data, so each person gets the message that fits where they are.

• Test everything: timing, subject lines, offers, channels. Keep what wins and kill what doesn't.

• Own deliverability, list health and the reporting that ties every flow to revenue.

What We’re Looking For

• Hands-on lifecycle or CRM experience at a consumer subscription app, with revenue results you can show.

• You've built flows yourself in a modern messaging platform like Braze, Customer.io, Iterable or Klaviyo.

• Strong with data. You build your own segments and read your own results without waiting for an analyst.

• You understand compliant communication for a global audience: consent, unsubscribes, GDPR, CAN-SPAM and their equivalents.

• You write good copy, or know exactly how to brief and edit it.

• You shape the strategy and do the implementation yourself.

• Excellent written English.

Bonus Points

• In-app messaging and push experience on iOS and Android.

• Deliverability experience: domain reputation, warming, and bringing a large dormant list back safely.

• Experience with web and app subscription billing and the events it sends.

• You've worked on a product where trust and tone really matter.

What You’ll Get

• Flexible job schedule and generous vacation policy.

• Direct impact on millions of worldwide users within months.

• Push the boundaries of applied AI in a consumer setting.

• Fully remote, able to work CET hours.

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/replika-lifecycle-crm-specialist

In 1977, Charles and Ray Eames began a film with a picnic beside Chicago’s lakefront. Over the next nine minutes, Powers of Ten traveled out toward distant galaxies and back into the microscopic world inside a human hand. An enormous subject became a journey you could follow, built around a simple change in perspective. Images, language, movement, and sound brought the idea to life together.

That’s the kind of creative thinking we’re looking for at Mercury: finding a compelling idea inside something complex, then bringing together the people and crafts that make it unforgettable.

We’re looking for a Creative Director to build and lead Brand Narrative , a new team within Brand Creative. You’ll turn company strategy, product truths, customer insight, and cultural observations into original concepts for our most important launches, campaigns, and brand moments. You’ll originate ideas yourself and stay closely involved as they become finished work.

Your background might be in art direction, design, or copywriting. What matters is your ability to develop exceptional concepts, recognize the best idea wherever it comes from, and bring the whole creative studio together to make it real. Whatever your starting discipline, you’ll bring deep experience in film-led storytelling.

You’ll lead Brand Narrative in close creative partnership with your peers leading Brand Design and Writing. Together, you’ll shape concepts, language, and visual expression from the beginning, bringing distinct perspectives and shared ownership to the work. You’ll contribute strong ideas of your own, invite others to challenge and improve them, and build on theirs. This is a role for someone who enjoys making work together, not developing ideas in isolation and handing them off.

You’ll also shape what Brand Narrative becomes. That means building its culture, developing its people, and establishing ways of working that make the entire studio more creatively ambitious. The opportunity is to make great work while building a team that can keep making it.

What you’ll do

In your first year, your focus will be roughly 70% leading creative development for our highest-priority launches and campaigns, and 30% building the Brand Narrative function.

• Originate and lead big creative ideas. Partner with Product Marketing and Brand Marketing on the brief, then turn the agreed audience, opportunity, and product proof into original creative concepts. Develop ideas that can take distinctive forms across film, social, out-of-home, digital, experiences, and partnerships.

• Bring ambitious concepts to life with your creative peers and the full studio. Work side by side with the Brand Design and Writing leads and their teams from the earliest explorations through delivery. Develop ideas together, exchange thoughtful critique, and make creative choices that draw on each discipline’s expertise. Stay hands-on, contribute through your own craft, and partner closely with Motion and Production throughout. For film, remain closely involved through scripts, visual development, production, and the final edit.

• Build audience and distribution thinking into the idea. Shape concepts around how people will discover, watch, and share the work. Work with marketing partners to consider channels and viewing contexts from the beginning, so the work belongs where people encounter it rather than simply being resized to fit.

• Push beyond the first good answer, and learn quickly. Lead thoughtful concept development and critique. Use rough scripts, prototypes, and AI tools to test ideas quickly, learn, and move the strongest work forward. Know when to keep exploring and when to commit, then protect what makes an idea interesting through feedback and production.

• Find opportunities before a brief arrives. Bring curiosity about Mercury’s products, customers, and the wider world. Develop proactive ideas and cultural opportunities that give the brand something meaningful to say or do.

• Help decide where creative ambition matters most. Partner early with Product Marketing, Brand Marketing, Product Design, Comms, and Insights. Help identify which moments deserve our largest creative investment, present recommendations to senior leadership, and use results from marketing and insights partners to inform what comes next.

• Build and lead Brand Narrative. Define the team’s purpose, priorities, creative standards, and ways of working. Help hire and develop the team, shaping its structure and capabilities. Set clear expectations, and coach people to grow their judgment and conceptual strength.

• Create a culture where the best idea wins. Make room for experimentation, honest feedback, and contributions across disciplines. Lead with generosity and conviction, share ownership of the work, and help people challenge one another without making creativity a competition for credit.

About Upsun

Upsun is the cloud application platform humans and robots love. It’s built for hybrid teams, where AI agents write and test code and people focus on the problems that really matter. Developers, DevOps engineers, and platform teams use Upsun to build, ship, and scale with confidence, without wrestling with backend infrastructure.

Upsun Dispatch, our newest offering, brings that same idea to the whole team. It’s the platform for governed collaboration between AI agents and cross-functional humans. Agents handle the volume in isolated sandboxes. People make the decisions that matter, with every approval and every cost on the record.

We give you your time back. You get:

• Predictable performance, even at scale

• Secure, compliant environments by default

• Real-time observability and profiling built in

• Cloning, configuration, and provisioning in seconds

• AI-ready features that plug directly into your stack

The name says it all. “Up” stands for uptime, reliability, and acceleration. “Sun” reflects our follow-the-sun support: a 24x7, globally distributed team keeping the lights on while you rest. We believe software should power brighter solutions and greater innovation.

Upsunners are a remote, global team, and we thrive in a multicultural one. We’re committed to open source and an open, welcoming environment, and our people span the whole experience spectrum. What ties us together is curiosity, a thirst for knowledge, and an eagerness for new ideas and cultures. We believe we can build anything together when the environment frees you to do your best work.

Our values:
We make a positive impact.
We aim for the stars.
We care for each other.

Impact of a Director, Product-Led Growth

As Director, PLG, you’ll lead the strategy, execution, and commercial success of Upsun’s product-led revenue engine. Upsun is expanding its portfolio with Upsun Dispatch , a strategic new offer that joins Upsun Cloud, and this role will turn that expansion into measurable growth.

Reporting directly to the Chief Marketing Officer, you will own the revenue target for product-led experiences, building a scalable engine across developer recruitment, freemium conversion, and customer retention. Working at the intersection of Marketing, Product Management, and Engineering, you will bridge technical platform capabilities with market-driven execution to scale Upsun’s global footprint.

What to expect

•
Own product-led revenue: Be accountable for ARR from self-serve experiences, from first signup through conversion, expansion, and retention.

•
Drive growth goals: Build and execute PLG programs to achieve clear top-line ARR milestones and hit aggressive user acquisition targets with specific focus in Europe and North America.

•

•
Strategic judgment: Ability to turn complex developer platform capabilities into intuitive self-service user experiences that drive clear, measurable business value.

•
Cross-functional execution: A record of leading cross-functional growth initiatives across Marketing, Product Management, and Engineering.

Data-driven approach: Hands-on depth in growth analytics, conversion funnels, freemium-to-paid activation, and retention.

Global scale: Scaling product-led revenue across remote-first, international teams.

At Upsun, remote work isn't just a trend - it's our foundation. The freedom of remote work with the support of a diverse, global team has been our successful model for over a decade. jobs.sourceName: RSS: We Work Remotely: All Other
jobs.description:
Headquarters: United States

URL: https://www.trmlabs.com/

About the Role

When a protocol is drained, or an exchange is compromised, our customers need to know within minutes or hours which addresses to block and where the funds are going. You will own TRM's answer to that, end-to-end.

As a Senior / Staff Threat Intelligence Analyst , you will lead TRM's hacks category: the metrics, the system that hits them, and the small contractor team that keeps it running around the clock. We align on the outcome; the approach is yours.

The impact you will have

•
Take command when a big hack breaks and act as a leader. Run the response: triage, coordination across teams, internal and customer communications, and the incident report afterwards.

•
Get every major hack into TRM fast. Make sure every major hack is visible to customers within hours of the first credible public report, around the clock.

•
Keep TRM's hack data complete and accurate. Every hack, at any size, is recorded with its entity, theft addresses, date, amount, and hack type.

•
Follow the money at scale. Design the system, with our Data Science and engineering teams, that carries hack-specific attribution downstream as stolen funds move.

•
Build the machine with AI. Leverage AI to build the tools and agents to automate key parts of hacks analysis and response, while ensuring human quality control over every output.

•
Explain how it happened. Root-cause the most important hacks and publish best-in-industry technical analysis that makes TRM the first source cited.

•
See the next one coming. Build approaches that spot vulnerable contracts before they are exploited, and get them into our product.

What we're looking for

•
5+ years of professional experience in blockchain intelligence, crypto investigations, cyber threat intelligence, incident response, or a closely related field.

•
Has owned incident response in a high-stakes environment (exchange, security firm, incident response, or CTI team): war rooms, incident reports, communications under pressure.

•
Strong blockchain tracing across major chains (BTC, EVM, TRON, Solana), including bridges, cross-chain swaps, and mixers.

•
Understands how DeFi, bridge, and exchange exploits work, and how attackers behave after the theft.

•
Applied AI fluency. We expect you to already be building AI-assisted or agentic workflows in your daily analytical work, to be able to show how you validate their outputs and where they fail, and to treat AI as a force multiplier.

•
Experience managing contractors or leading a small team.

•
Writes and briefs clearly, from technical deep-dives to executive summaries.

•
Hands-on and highly accountable: does the hardest work, not only coordinates it.

Nice to have

•
Smart-contract reverse-engineering (Solidity).

•
Experience at a security auditor or blockchain analytics firm.

•
Experience following specific well-known hacker groups.

About the Team

The hacks function sits within TRM's Primary Intelligence organization, alongside the Facilitation & Money Laundering (F&ML) pod. You will work closely with the Nation States, Cyber Threat Intelligence, and Global Investigations teams, as well as with Data Science and Engineering on automation, and with Marketing on publications.

Team Operating Rhythms

•
Monthly metrics review with your manager.

•
Weekly operating sync with your team.

•
Regular syncs with your team across time zones.

•
A war room, run by you, whenever a major hack breaks.

•
On-call responsibilities

Application Instructions

If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.

Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your skills and qualifications for the role.

If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure your application will be considered.

Interviewing with TRM

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while allowing you to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, an AI skills assessment, and a Leadership Principles interview.

•
Recruiter Intro: Qualifications, motivations, and alignment with the role.

•
Hiring Manager: Deep dive into your relevant experience, skills, and impact.

•
First Round: 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role.

•
Final Round: Hands-on case study. This is usually a panel-style session where we go deeper into your craft, problem-solving, and alignment with TRM.

•
References: Former colleagues who can provide insight into your work and impact.

•
Offer: Congrats! Your recruiter will present the offer and compensation details.

•

Headquarters: Remote - US

Who We Are

Oportun (Nasdaq: OPRT) is a mission-driven financial services company that puts its members' financial goals within reach. With intelligent borrowing, savings, and budgeting capabilities, Oportun empowers members with the confidence to build a better financial future. Since inception, Oportun has provided more than $22.7 billion in responsible and affordable credit, saved its members more than $2.5 billion in interest and fees, and helped its members set aside an average of more than $1,800 annually.

The Opportunity

As part of the Collections team, the Repossession Coordinator manages key activities across Oportun’s repossession and remarketing process, supporting members with delinquent accounts while coordinating timely, accurate actions with internal partners and third-party vendors. Success in this role means maintaining strong operational controls, clear communication, accurate account and inventory reviews, and adherence to applicable lending regulations and Oportun policies.

At Oportun, we move fast and we hold each other to a high bar. If you care about doing your best work while actually moving the needle for real people, you'll fit right in.

What You'll Do

Your day-to-day

• You'll provide support and guidance to members with delinquent accounts who may be eligible for repossession, ensuring clear and respectful communication throughout the process.

• You'll coordinate repossession and remarketing activities with members, internal business partners, and third-party vendors to support timely and accurate execution.

• You'll complete required account reviews, letters, scrubs, and other operational steps associated with repossession and remarketing.

• You'll monitor repossession and remarketing inventory and account status, identifying issues and escalating or routing them accurately to the appropriate partners.

• You'll communicate and collaborate effectively with business partners to resolve workflow issues and keep repossession and remarketing activities moving.

• You'll maintain current knowledge of applicable lending regulations and Oportun policies and apply them consistently in day-to-day work.

Who You Are

The right fit looks like this

• You're detail-oriented, organized, and comfortable managing multiple priorities in a regulated operational environment.

• You solve problems thoughtfully, communicate clearly with members and partners, and know when an issue needs to be escalated.

• You're comfortable navigating complexity and don't wait for perfect information to move forward.

• You're comfortable navigating complexity and don't wait for perfect information to move forward. You communicate clearly, give direct feedback, and expect the same in return.

What You Bring

Skills & experience

Required

• You'll have 5–7 years of collections experience.

• You'll have 5–7 years of repossession experience.

• You've demonstrated strong problem-solving skills, attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple priorities.

• You communicate effectively and collaborate with members, business partners, and third-party vendors. You bring working knowledge of applicable lending regulations and the ability to follow established policies and procedures.

Nice to Have

• Bilingual communication skills.

• Experience supporting vehicle remarketing processes.

• Familiarity with tools or systems used to manage collections, repossession, remarketing, or inventory workflows.

• You've used AI tools (ChatGPT, Copilot, or similar) to improve your own productivity.

Our AI Mindset

We build with AI. We lead with judgment.

AI isn't a feature here. It's how we work.

We're excited about what AI makes possible, and we're looking for people who share that curiosity. You don't need to be an expert. You need to be open to experimenting , willing to learn, and able to apply new tools in ways that actually move the needle.

In this role, you'll be encouraged to explore AI tools, find practical use cases for your function, and bring ideas for working smarter. We believe the best outcomes come when human judgment and AI capability work together .

jobs.title: Principal Experience Designer - Visual Design & Design Systems
jobs.sourceName: RSS: We Work Remotely: Design
jobs.description:
Headquarters: United States

URL: https://www.workiva.com/latam/

Workiva is looking for a Principal Experience Designer to shape the visual future of Unify, our enterprise design system. Unify powers the components, patterns, templates, accessibility standards, and shared experiences used across Workiva’s B2B platform.

This is a dual-focus principal role. Roughly 60–70% of your time will be spent leading Unify’s visual design direction: evolving its visual language, shaping token architecture, and creating the reference designs and guidance that help teams build consistently. The remaining 30–40% will focus on high-visibility visual work for major conferences, marketing partnerships, and executive audiences. That work is not separate from the system, it’s part of the broader ecosystem of design in which Unify lives.

You will bring exceptional visual craft, strong systems thinking, and a practical point of view on how design systems need to evolve for AI-assisted design and prototyping.

What you’ll do

• Define and evolve Unify’s visual language across typography, color, spacing, iconography, motion, and brand expression.

• Partner with the components sub-team and the patterns and templates sub-team to ensure visual design is applied consistently and intentionally across every asset.

• Partner with product design, product mgmt and engineering teams to ensure product experience decisions translate faithfully from system to production.

• Maintain a scalable, semantic token architecture that supports consistent experiences across products and over time.

• Create and maintain a library of reference designs, full-screen examples that demonstrate how Unify should be applied in real product experiences.

• Own visual usage guidance and documentation that make intended use, constraints, and quality standards clear for designers, engineers, and AI-assisted workflows.

• Establish ongoing evaluation of AI-generated designs and prototypes, using what you learn to strengthen tokens, examples, and guidance before inconsistencies reach product teams.

• Lead visual design for select high-stakes moments, including major conferences, executive presentations, product vision work, and marketing partnerships.

• Coach designers and influence cross-functional partners through high-quality feedback, clear principles, and strong visual storytelling.

What you’ll need

Minimum Qualifications

• 10+ years of experience in product design, visual design, UX, or related fields, including significant work on platform or enterprise products.

• Bachelor's degree in Design, HCI, or a related field (or 8 years of experience and a Master's degree; or a PhD with 6 years of experience).

Preferred Qualifications

• A portfolio demonstrating exceptional visual craft and the ability to translate a visual point of view into scalable product systems.

• Hands-on experience with AI-assisted design or prototyping workflows, with a clear perspective on their opportunities and limitations.

• Experience defining or evolving a design system’s visual language, including tokens, components, patterns, and documentation.

• Strong ability to create compelling product narratives for senior leaders and high-visibility audiences.

• Experience partnering closely with engineers and working through the tradeoffs between design intent, system health, and implementation.

• A track record of influencing and coaching teams without relying on formal authority.

• Experience building reference sites, design-system documentation, or machine-readable design guidance.

• Experience with semantic or multi-tier token systems, motion design, presentation design, or event experiences.

• Background in front-end development, developer tools, cross-platform systems, or highly regulated industries.

Travel Requirements & Working Conditions

• Up to 20-25% travel required to meet with teams, partners, and customers

• Reliable internet connection required for remote or hybrid work environments

How You’ll Be Rewarded

✅ Salary range in the US: $190,000.00 - $315,000.00

✅ A discretionary bonus typically paid annually

✅ Restricted Stock Units granted at time of hire

✅ 401(k) match and comprehensive employee benefits package

The salary range represents the low and high end of the salary range for this job in the US. Minimums and maximums may vary based on location. The actual salary offer will carefully consider a wide range of factors, including your skills, qualifications, experience and other relevant factors.
